rv.q: Julia Roberts/Richard Gere rom-com is a triumph of exuberant zest over dodgy subject matter.
Fans can rest assured that the show follows the film faithfully.
If you’re seeking to relive popcorn memories, you will have fun muttering along with the romcom’s snappiest lines.
But the musical does deliver what many will be after: a fun retread of swooned-over movie moments.
It can’t decide if it is a straight rip-off of the film (80% of the time) or a more imaginative, theatrical, quirky affair.
This is nostalgia-by-numbers padded out with ballads, as cynical as it is icky.
After that you're out on the sidewalk, feeling (unless you're the most forgiving and/or financially well-endowed fan) pretty fleeced.
There might be a version of Pretty Woman that you could do now, but this isn’t it.
This feels like a shallow and at times tasteless show but, within the rules of a romcom, it works in its central, schmaltzy storyline of love despite the odds.
Bringing it to the West End in this shape was a big mistake.
In fact, ‘Pretty Woman: The Musical’ is so witless that it defies any serious attempt to scrutinise its politics.
This production has been designed for a fanbase that has existed for decades, and which expects particular lines, costumes and scenes that replicate the movie.
He ups the energy and momentum throughout.
Director Jerry Mitchell started life as a choreographer and it shows.
Pretty Woman won't be the last cynical miscalculation to hit the West End, but if it brings Harms to a broader public, well, no harm done there.
That it simply wants to be a facsimile of a once popular movie, reveals the ugliness at its core.
Either way, this startlingly dull show, with forgettable songs by Bryan Adams, is low-hanging fruit when it comes to criticising its attitudes towards sex, women and money.

cn.t: Critics find this musical adaptation of the beloved 1990 film largely superfluous and dated, though some praise the leads' chemistry and Bryan Adams' rock score. Most question its #MeToo-era relevance, calling it a calculated cash-in.
